payment.title: Payment Service Troubleshooting Playbook
steps: 1. Check payment service health: curl https://monitoring.internal/api/health/payment
2. Review error logs: grep ERROR /var/log/payment-service/app.log
3. Check DB connection pool utilization via Grafana dashboard
4. Verify upstream payment processor status at https://status.stripe.com
5. Check if recent deployment occurred: kubectl rollout history deploy/payment-service
6. Test backup gateway: curl -X POST https://payment-bkp.internal/v1/charge
7. Enable failover if backup gateway is healthy: kubectl set env deploy/payment-service PAYMENT_FAILOVER=true
8. If error rate over 50%, consider rolling back last deployment
9. Escalate to #payment-oncall if unresolved after 15 minutes

database.title: Database Troubleshooting Playbook
steps: 1. Check database connectivity: psql -h db.internal -U app_user -c SELECT 1
2. Check active connections: SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state=active
3. Check for long-running queries: SELECT pid, now()-query_start, query FROM pg_stat_activity
4. Check disk space: df -h /var/lib/postgresql
5. Review slow query log
6. Kill blocking queries if necessary: SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid)
7. Escalate to #db-oncall if unresolved

auth.title: Authentication Service Troubleshooting Playbook
steps: 1. Check auth service health: curl https://auth.internal/health
2. Test login flow with test credentials
3. Check Redis connectivity: redis-cli -h cache.internal ping
4. Check Redis memory: redis-cli -h cache.internal info memory
5. Review auth service logs for error patterns
6. Verify JWT_SECRET is consistent across all pods
7. Restart auth pods if Redis was recovered
8. Escalate to #identity-oncall if login success rate under 90%

notification.title: Notification Service Troubleshooting Playbook
steps: 1. Check notification service health: curl https://notifications.internal/health
2. Check email queue depth via admin API
3. Verify SMTP connectivity: telnet smtp.internal 587
4. Check APNS certificate for iOS push: openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in apns.pem
5. Verify FCM API key validity for Android push
6. Review notification service error logs
7. Test sending a single notification manually via admin API
8. Escalate to #notifications-oncall if delivery rate under 80%

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure Troubleshooting Playbook
steps: 1. Check cluster health: kubectl get nodes
2. Check pod status: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | grep -v Running
3. Check load balancer status in cloud console
4. Verify health check endpoints are responding: curl -f http://instance-ip/health
5. Check disk space on nodes: kubectl top nodes
6. Review cluster events: kubectl get events --all-namespaces
7. Escalate to #sre-oncall for critical infrastructure issues

general.title: General Incident Troubleshooting Playbook
steps: 1. Identify the affected service and check its health endpoint
2. Review recent deployments in the last 2 hours
3. Check error rate and latency metrics in Grafana
4. Review application error logs for error patterns
5. Check upstream dependencies are healthy
6. Check infrastructure health (CPU, memory, disk, network)
7. Identify if there is a recent config change
8. Apply relevant workaround if available
9. Escalate to service owner if unresolved after 15 minutes
10. For P1: create incident bridge and notify stakeholders
